# The CLI reads method and type names from the adapter; Program.cs is tidy
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #171, sha256:a00b7070322b9ef29162289f4be664acd61fa104d58c6e61869c80d70c05e688). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** tooling (thin slice; split from card 161 by Decider D113)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Decider D113 (2026-10-28): card 161 closes on its core outcome and the remaining review findings become small separate cards, each reviewable and revertable on its own. Two independent reviews of card 161 asked for this work.
- **Depends on:** 161
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want the command line to know nothing about the C# layout, so that a second adapter does not need changes in the CLI.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a build, When the CLI writes the map, Then csMethod and the generated type names come from the output the adapter returned (per endpoint and phrase, like the file paths), with no hardcoded Handler or Phrases names in the CLI
  2. Given Program.cs, When it is read, Then it has one statement per line, no one-line nested loops, no long chained statements, and no null-forgiving operators
  3. Given the generated C# for orders and the demo, When the card is merged, Then it is byte-identical to before (the recorded hash is unchanged)

## Context

- Dependency direction: lower layers never know about higher ones; the CLI is higher than the adapter. Follow docs/CODING_GUIDELINES.md: one required test per criterion, shown failing first; the generated C# output stays identical (the recorded orders hash stays 409bf3c6...).
